name: Shimei
overview: Shimei was a male Levite identified as the son of Ladan, as he was included among the 'fathers' households of Ladan' in 1 Chronicles 23:9. His lineage places him within the tribe of Levi, which held significant religious responsibilities in Israel. Beyond this genealogical note, Scripture provides no additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimei means 'YHWH has heard' or 'famous,' reflecting a Hebrew origin and possibly indicating a recognition of God's attentiveness or renown. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:9, was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological implication consistent with Levite heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Shimei had fathers named Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, as noted in 1 Chronicles 23:9. These relationships situate him within a specific family branch of the Levites connected to Ladan. No further family relationships are recorded beyond these paternal connections.
scriptureSignificance: Shimei's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the Levitical families, which were entrusted with sacred duties in Israel's worship system. Being listed among the 'fathers' households of Ladan highlights his role in the organization of Levitical service during King David's time. Although not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion reflects the careful record-keeping of those set apart for God's service, underscoring the importance of lineage in fulfilling divine purposes.
